source.title: Current challenges and future directions in Achilles tendon rupture repair: A biomechanical perspective

paper.citation: Xu R., Song Z., Hou T., Yang H., An Z., Yao Y., et al. Current challenges and future directions in Achilles tendon rupture repair: A biomechanical perspective. Journal of Biomechanics. 2026;204:113347. doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2026.113347.
paper.abstract: This paper addresses the following question: How do macro-, micro-, and nanoscale Achilles tendon structures support mechanical function, what limits current rupture-repair strategies, and what design priorities should guide tissue-engineered scaffolds? Participants: No new human cohort; narrative synthesis of human, animal, mechanical, and tissue-engineering research. Sport and level: Achilles rupture across clinical and sports contexts; not restricted to athletes or a competition level. Design: Interdisciplinary narrative review. Exposure or intervention: Conservative/surgical repair and tissue-engineered scaffold strategies.
paper.tldr: The review describes native Achilles tendon as a multiscale system of twisting tripartite subtendons, hierarchical collagen fibers, and quarter-staggered/cross-linked collagen that supports nonlinear and negative-Poisson-ratio behavior. Cited estimates indicate Achilles loading of 2.70–3.95 times body weight during walking and >12 times body weight during running. Use this paper to understand the biological/mechanical reasons that tendon length, stiffness, and functional capacity may remain altered after rupture.
paper.methods: Design: Interdisciplinary narrative review. Exposure or intervention: Conservative/surgical repair and tissue-engineered scaffold strategies. Comparator: Native tendon multiscale architecture/mechanics versus healed tendon and scaffold designs. Measurements and outcomes: Tendon geometry, collagen organization/cross-linking, nonlinear mechanics, Poisson behavior, mechanical compatibility, and regenerative function. Analysis: Narrative integration of biomechanics, materials science, and tissue engineering; no stated systematic-search or risk-of-bias method.
paper.findings: The review describes native Achilles tendon as a multiscale system of twisting tripartite subtendons, hierarchical collagen fibers, and quarter-staggered/cross-linked collagen that supports nonlinear and negative-Poisson-ratio behavior. Cited estimates indicate Achilles loading of 2.70–3.95 times body weight during walking and >12 times body weight during running. The authors report conventional treatment limitations, including a cited conservative-treatment rerupture rate up to 20.8% and suboptimal large-gap outcomes after suturing. Existing scaffold research is largely single-scale and does not simultaneously restore macroscopic support, microscopic compatibility, and nanoscale bioactivity/mechanics.
paper.limitations: No systematic search, study-quality appraisal, or pooled clinical outcomes were reported; the review's conclusions are mechanistic and research-oriented. Evidence spans species, scales, and laboratory methods, so material/scaffold findings cannot be assumed to improve human return to sport. Cross-scale structure–mechanics relationships and standardized measurement remain incomplete, and proposed scaffolds are not established clinical solutions. Additional transfer limitation — interpretation: The review does not define loading progression, clearance criteria, or treatment selection for an individual athlete.
paper.practicalImplications: Use this paper to understand the biological/mechanical reasons that tendon length, stiffness, and functional capacity may remain altered after rupture. Do not translate its scaffold proposals into current rehabilitation practice; athlete management should rely on clinical repair status, progressive loading, symptoms, function, and established return-to-sport evidence.
